where: Section 1, paragraph on recursion and IIR
problem: The text says that if at least one a_k is nonzero the impulse response lasts forever, so the system is IIR. A recursive equation can still have a finite impulse response when a pole cancels a zero (for example y[n] = x[n] − 0.5x[n−1] + 0.5y[n−1] has h[n] = δ[n]). The absolute statement will be marked wrong by a strict examiner.
fix: Add the caveat: 'Recursive usually means IIR. A zero that exactly cancels a pole makes the impulse response finite even though the equation is recursive.'

problem: The sentence mixes two realisations. It claims N delays, one adder and up to N + M + 1 multipliers. The count N + M + 1 multipliers with a single adder belongs to direct form II, which needs max(N, M) delays, not N. Direct form I needs N + M delays and two adders. Section 1 also says the number of unit delays in the hardware equals N, which fails when M > N.
fix: Write: 'Direct form II uses max(N, M) delays and one summing node; direct form I uses N + M delays and two adders. Both need up to N + M + 1 multipliers.' In Section 1, say the stored past outputs number N, and the delays in a canonical realisation number max(N, M).

problem: The rule 'a constant input gives a constant guess A' fails when the input has the same form as a natural mode, for example a constant input when λ = 1 is a root, or an input 2ⁿ when λ = 2 is a root. Substituting the guess then gives 0 = 1 and the student is stuck.
fix: Add: 'If the guessed form already appears among the natural modes, multiply the guess by n (and by n again for a double repeat) before substituting.'

problem: The prose drops the subscripts and superscripts, so terms read as 'Ciλin', 'Cr−1nr−1' and 'multiplying by λN'. A student can read these as products of separate letters instead of C_i times λ_i to the power n.
fix: Use the inline tags: C<sub>i</sub>λ<sub>i</sub><sup>n</sup>, (C₀ + C₁n + … + C<sub>r−1</sub>n<sup>r−1</sup>)λ<sup>n</sup>, and 'multiplying by λ<sup>N</sup>'.

where: Section 1, opening of the standard form
problem: The sentence says that writing every output on the left and every input on the right gives the standard form, but the formula displayed already has y[n] alone on the left with the feedback terms moved to the right. The words describe one arrangement and the formula shows another.
fix: Say: 'Collecting output terms on the left and input terms on the right gives Σ<sub>k=0…N</sub> a<sub>k</sub> y[n − k] = Σ<sub>m=0…M</sub> b<sub>m</sub> x[n − m] with a₀ = 1. Solving for y[n] gives the recursive form used for computation:'
